extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_short: claiming foreign priority in US patents
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for claiming the benefit of the filing date of a prior foreign (or international) application in a U.S. nonprovisional patent application under 35 U.S.C. §§119, 120, 365 and applicable PCT/37 CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for benefit of prior foreign filing (general list)
rubrics_metrics.description: The conditions for benefit of the filing date of a prior foreign application: (A) foreign application filed in a country affording similar privileges or in a WTO member country; (B) filed by same applicant (inventor) or legal representatives/assigns; (C) U.S. application (or earliest parent under 35 U.S.C.120) filed within 12 months of earliest foreign filing; (D) foreign application must be for the same invention; (E) for original 35 U.S.C.111(a) applications (other than designs) filed on/after Nov 29, 2000, priority claim must be presented during pendency and within later of four months from actual U.S. filing date or 16 months from foreign filing date (non-extendable); (F) for national stage entries from international applications filed on/after Nov 29, 2000, after compliance with 35 U.S.C.371, the priority claim must be made during pendency and within PCT time limits; (G) when the basis is an application for an inventor's certificate, requirements of 37 CFR 1.55(b) must also be met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enumerated checklist is the primary set of substantive conditions to establish priority benefit. Note exceptions for design applications (6 months) and special procedural timing rules for PCT/national stage and post-November 29, 2000 filings. The timing in (E) is strict and not extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12‑month priority period (and 6‑month design exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States nonprovisional application (or its earliest parent under 35 U.S.C.120) must be filed within 12 months of the earliest foreign filing; the first day is not counted. The period of 12 months is 6 months in the case of designs (35 U.S.C.172).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: foreign filing on January 3, 1983 allows U.S. filing on January 3, 1984. If the 12th month last day is a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday in D.C., filing on the next business day is timely. Compute periods per Paris Convention Article 4C(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognized countries requirement and basis codes
rubrics_metrics.description: The foreign application must be filed in a foreign country which affords similar privileges to U.S. nationals (or in a WTO member country) — i.e., a 'recognized' country as listed in the Manual. The listing uses letters indicating the legal basis: 'I' = Paris Convention, 'P' = Inter‑American Convention, 'L' = reciprocal legislation, 'W' = WTO membership, 'W°' = joined WTO after Jan 1, 1996.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant asserts benefit based on a country not on the list, the examiner should contact the Office of International Relations to verify status. The right is based on the country of filing, not the applicant's citizenship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim form and required information
rubrics_metrics.description: A priority claim need not be in any special form; it may be a statement signed by a registered attorney or agent and can be made on filing by including a copy of an (un)executed oath/declaration specifying foreign priority (37 CFR 1.63(c)(2)) or by submitting an application data sheet specifying the foreign priority claim (37 CFR 1.76). Required information includes the application number and filing date of the foreign application, name of the treaty (if applicable), and name/location of the authority that received the foreign application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure the priority claim supplies the basic identifying data; use form paragraph (MPEP) where appropriate. For PCT-based priority, a declaration of the claim at time of filing (PCT Article 8(1), Rule 4.10) is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copy requirement for priority papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require the applicant to furnish a certified copy of the priority papers (35 U.S.C.119(b)(3)). Applicants must submit the certified copy of the foreign application specified in 35 U.S.C.119(b) or PCT Rule 17 before the patent is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the claim or certified copy is filed after payment of the issue fee, it must be accompanied by the processing fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i); the patent will not include the priority claim unless corrected by certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C.255 and 37 CFR 1.323. Certification by an authority designated under a treaty will satisfy the requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity of inventors requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventors of the U.S. nonprovisional application and the foreign application must be the same; right of priority does not exist if inventor A filed abroad and inventor B filed in the U.S., even if ownership is the same. The foreign application may, however, have been filed by the assignee, legal representative, or agent instead of the inventor, provided the inventor is identified in the foreign file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An indication of inventor identity in the U.S. oath/declaration identifying the foreign application and stating it was filed by the assignee/representative/agent is acceptable. Joint inventors can each claim benefit of their respective foreign applications for their common U.S. application (see MPEP §605.07).

rubrics_metrics.name: First foreign application (first‑to‑file) rule and post‑dating/post-withdrawal nuances
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority is measured from the first foreign application filed. If multiple foreign filings exist and the first was more than 12 months before the U.S. filing, no priority benefit is available. Post-dating (changing a filing date later) in some countries does not affect priority status. Public Law 87-333 extends priority in some circumstances where an earlier-filed application was withdrawn/abandoned under certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the first foreign filing was in a non-recognized country it is disregarded for priority purposes. If a later foreign application within 12 months discloses additional subject matter, claims limited to that additional matter may get the later foreign filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference of foreign priority application
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may incorporate by reference a foreign priority application by including an explicit statement in the U.S. application-as-filed that specifically enumerated foreign priority applications are 'hereby incorporated by reference.' For U.S. applications filed on or after Sep 21, 2004, the statement must appear in the specification (37 CFR 1.57(b) and MPEP §608.01(p)). For earlier filings, it could appear in the transmittal letter or specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporation by reference permits amendment of the U.S. application to include subject matter from the foreign application without raising new-matter issues, subject to the limits of 37 CFR 1.57(a) for inadvertently omitted material. Applicants are encouraged to provide explicit incorporation statements for applications filed on/after Sep 21, 2004 if they do not want the incorporation limited to inadvertently omitted material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of priority vis‑à‑vis intervening references and 35 U.S.C.102(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to rely on the foreign filing can overcome the effect of intervening references or uses, but the 1‑year bar of 35 U.S.C.102(b) is measured from the U.S. filing date, not the foreign filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a foreign filing in Jan 1982 and a U.S. filing in Dec 1982 cannot avoid a printed publication or public use that occurred in Nov 1981 (more than one year before the U.S. filing). Use priority to antedate references only to the extent permitted by statute and case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority based on inventor's certificate (37 CFR 1.55(b) / 35 U.S.C.119(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may claim priority based on an application for an inventor's certificate in countries that grant both inventor's certificates and patents, but when doing so must include an affidavit/declaration stating that, to the best of the applicant's knowledge, the applicant had the option to file either a patent or an inventor's certificate for the subject matter forming the basis of the priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit is limited to ascertaining whether applicants generally had the option in the country of filing; it is not intended to probe individual eligibility. Priority on inventor's certificates is honored only when the applicant had the discretion to choose patent vs. inventor's certificate. Effective date: 37 CFR 1.55(b) applied starting Aug 25, 1973.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT/international application priority entitlement (35 U.S.C.365)
rubrics_metrics.description: A national application shall be entitled to the right of priority based on a prior-filed international application which designated at least one country other than the United States (35 U.S.C.365). An international application designating the U.S. may be entitled to the right of priority of a prior foreign application (35 U.S.C.365(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The substantive right of priority under 365 derives from Paris Convention Article 4. Compliance with PCT treaty and regulations (declaration of priority at filing, etc.) is required to avoid rejection of the claim. The formal requirements may differ somewhat from those under 35 U.S.C.119(a)-(d) and (f).

rubrics_metrics.name: International application considered as national filing for priority purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application designating a country is considered to be a national application regularly filed in that country as of the international filing date, regardless of where it was physically filed or whether it was filed with an intergovernmental organization acting as a Receiving Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore, later national or international filings can claim benefit of the international filing date if conditions of 35 U.S.C.120 are met. If relying on an international application which designated but did not originate in the U.S., the Director may require a certified copy and an English translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT Rule 17 — obligation and timing to submit priority document
rubrics_metrics.description: Where priority of an earlier national or international application is claimed under Article 8, a certified copy of that earlier application (the priority document) must be submitted to the International Bureau or receiving Office not later than 16 months after the priority date, unless it was already filed with the receiving Office. If received after the time limit but before international publication, the document is considered received on the last day of the time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the priority document was not filed with the receiving Office, timely submission to the IB (or request that the receiving Office transmit it) is mandatory. Missing the 16‑month deadline can risk loss of priority unless exceptional provisions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative submission/transmission of priority document (Rule 17(b) and (bbis))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the priority document is issued by the receiving Office, the applicant may instead request the receiving Office to prepare and transmit the priority document to the International Bureau (request due within 16 months and may be subject to a fee). If the priority document is available in a digital library per the Administrative Instructions, the applicant may request the receiving Office or International Bureau to obtain it from that digital library instead of submitting it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these alternatives when appropriate to avoid duplicate certified copy submissions and fees. Requests must be timely (within 16 months) and may incur receiving Office fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority document submission when requesting early processing (PCT Article 23(2) / Rule 17.1(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant requests early processing of the international application under PCT Article 23(2), the priority document must be submitted to the International Bureau at that time (Rule 17.1(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early processing requests change the timing requirements; ensure all priority documents accompany the early processing request to avoid noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority based on earlier international application does not require filing priority copy with IB
rubrics_metrics.description: If priority is based on an earlier international application, a copy need not be filed with the Receiving Office or the International Bureau because the IB already possesses that earlier international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces redundant submission for priority claims relying on earlier PCT filings that are in IB custody.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority may be based on utility model (Gebrauchsmuster)
rubrics_metrics.description: The right of priority can be based upon an application in a foreign country for a 'utility model' (e.g., Gebrauchsmuster in Germany).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat such utility model filings as qualifying earlier filings for priority subject to the same conditions (e.g., same invention, timing, recognized country).
